summary: Wave C biome-fire package, resumed after the 17:12 session kill. All five items are implemented and checked on Build/biome-fire (final build 19:13). The killed run had already written most of the work: FireComposite (branched layers, a tier split, a flame band in world units, a moving fill band), FireOverlay shape 3 (the spark), the FireBead fireball and the FireFx sparks. This run read all of it, compiled it (SetupAndCompile PASS, BuildWindows Success twice) and finished it. It added three things. (a) On the GLES3 path without Gather, the normal now comes from the per-pixel relief gradient where the relief slopes, with screen derivatives as the fallback (fix item 4 of the fill). (b) Below High, the fireball's luminance is capped at linear 0.7, so a light player color cannot outshine the spark. The human seat color comes from the shared SaveData choice, which another agent set to yellow, and a yellow fireball clipped to near white (spark ratio 0.82x on Low). (c) A new EditMode test compiles every subshader of the three fire graphs: target 2.0 for GLES3 and target 4.5 for D3D11, because ShaderCheck and a Windows build only compile the active one. Results: fire slope 2.59 ms/Mpix at Medium uncapped (target 2.95, baseline 4.34; liquid 1.84, fire/liquid 1.41, perfslope PASS, hash 246577239DE179C4 on every run). Fire Low avgMs is 3.43 to 3.84 against Medium 3.95 to 4.07 at 1080x1200 (baseline Low 7.49, Medium 6.05). Spark against fireball, Medium CutDroplets at 540x960: 3.86x with the orange human, 2.02x with the yellow human. Flame tongues reach 40 to 50 px above top edges and 10 to 20 px below bottom edges at 60 px/u (the critic measured 4 to 11 and 0). A 12 fps capture shows the white-hot band with its tongues sweeping the capture. Low draws cells instead of the value-noise lattice. The user likes fire because it spreads, so I judged the flame band and the fill front on screenshots at 540x960 (High, Medium and Low) and at 1080x2400 (High and Medium; the window was resized past the 1200 px monitor, and Medium renders at scale 0.667 there through the infra-perf cap). Tests: EditMode 488 run, 485 pass, 2 skipped, 1 failing (biome-electric-liquid's own WaveC_ElectricFill test, which that package is editing). The 7 WaveC_BiomeFire tests pass on the final sources, and PlayMode BootTests pass 4/4.

api_additions: FireFx.MaxFrontSparks = 20 (most live sparks in the shower of one live front; SparkRate 46 x SparkLifeMax 0.4 = 18.4 stays below)

FireFx.FillSparkRate = 42, FillSparkLifeMin = 0.25, FillSparkLifeMax = 0.5, FillFollowMargin = 0.2, MaxFills = 4 (sparks thrown up from the advancing front of a fill, found through TerritoryField.RevealTimeOf against RevealNow, inside the 200 particle cap)
FireOverlay.hlsl: PIO_FIRE_SPARK_DISC 0.12, PIO_FIRE_SPARK_CORONA 0.17, PIO_FIRE_SPARK_HALO 0.45 (world units, designed for RetractionView.GlintHalfSize 0.5)

FireComposite.hlsl: PIO_FireEdgeDistance (inverse normal CDF of the wide relief field, world distance to the contour), PIO_FireWideDistance, PIO_FireRevealAges, PIO_FireCells4, PIO_FireCellsStatic, PIO_FireTongue (file-local helpers, no shared signature changed)
contract_issues: 25.3 flame band: it is laid out in world units from the wide relief field (d = sigma x inverse normal CDF of max t_wide, sigma 0.267 u). Outward tongues reach 0.3 u on edges facing screen down and 0.85 u on edges facing up, +75 % while the fill gate is on. The reach is capped at 0.9 u on Medium and High (where the owner tap 0.35 u inward keeps the color) and at 0.55 u on Low. Inward tongues burn over the outer 0.42 to 0.5 u of the bed. The cellular coal mosaic, the pocket stripes without flames and the four distinct colors are kept.

25.2 / 25.3 fill front (fire): the flash exp(-age / 0.045) becomes a moving band. A Gaussian of the age centred at 0.08 s (width 0.08 s, zero after 0.3 s) only gates a white-hot band placed from the contour (about 0.14 u inside) plus taller tongues. Each texel's age is clamped to 0.4 s before interpolation (Gather), the jitter is at most 0.05 u, fresh embers settle within 0.8 s, and deeper than 0.2 u inside the age is read at each coal's centre. FillDuration 0.6 s, TerritoryField and the -1000 sentinel are unchanged.

25.5 spark (fire): FireOverlay shape 3 draws a solid white disc of radius 0.12 u (pale corona to 0.17 u) over a saturated orange halo #FF8A2A (radius 0.45 u, alpha 0.8, smooth falloff) with rays 1.5x longer. High keeps the HDR boost (5.2, 4.6, 3.6) for bloom. Below High, FireBead caps the fireball body and corona at linear luminance 0.7 (about 215 luma), keeping the hue, so the spark stays the brightest moving thing for every player color.

12.2 item 4 / quality tiers (fire): the tier split reads _PIO_Quality without touching QualityTier. High: B-spline territory, 3x3 animated coals, 3 flame octaves. Medium: bilinear, 2x2 animated coals (same coal identities), 2 octaves. Low: 2x2 static jittered Voronoi coals, 2 octaves on one warp, no owner or glow tap, no cracks. Twinkle is picked per coal and per third of a second on every tier. Medium fetch budget: 7 (territory, wide Gather, reveal Gather, pocket, actor, owner tap, actor glow tap).

25.5 FireFx: the advancing fill front throws up sparks (42 per second, life 0.25 to 0.5 s). The live fuse front keeps at most 20 live sparks (46 per second x 0.4 s) under its warm orange glow. Both stay inside the 200 cap.

failing: PainterIO.Tests.WaveC_BiomeElectricLiquidTests.WaveC_ElectricFill_ClampsTheAge_AndDrawsNoEdgeFromIt ('one use of _PIO_Now: expected 1, was 2'): biome-electric-liquid's own test on its own shader, which that package was editing and rebuilding during my run (Build/biome-electric-liquid build3 at 19:21). Not a biome-fire file.

items.evidence: FireComposite.hlsl branches every expensive layer coherently. (1) The coals and the ember bed run only where cT > 0. (2) The flame noise runs only inside the flame band (-reachIn < d < reachOut, player alive). (3) The reveal age with its jitter and the owner tap run only within 1.2 u of a bed. (4) The cracks run only where the bed does not cover, on rich tiers, under a sparse mask; their width is 0.012 + pix, so they need no fwidth. (5) Tier split as in contract_issues (High full stack, Medium 2 octaves and 2x2 coals, Low static cells). (6) The float hash was not needed. All ddx/ddy/fwidth calls sit at the top of the function and every fetch inside a branch is LOD 0 or a Gather: WaveC_FireShadersKeepDerivativesAndImplicitLodOutOfDynamicBranches parses every [branch] body of the three shaders and passes. WaveC_FireCompositeMediumFetchBudgetIsAtMostSeven passes. SetupAndCompile PASS (ShaderCheck, Logs/biome-fire_setup.log) and BuildWindows 'Build Finished, Result: Success' twice. The new WaveC_FireGraphsCompileOnEverySubshader compiles the forward pass of each subshader of FireComposite, FireOverlay and FireBead, GLES3x for target 2.0 and D3D11 for target 4.5, and passes: the GLES3 path without Gather compiles. Perf: 'verify.ps1 -Steps perfslope -ProbeExe Build/biome-fire/PainterIO.exe' PASS (docs/waveC/biome-fire/perf/biome-fire_perfslope.log). Slopes at Medium uncapped: liquid 1.84, fire 2.59, electric 2.02 ms/Mpix. Fire/liquid is 1.41. Best fire avgMs is 4.27 at 1080x1200 and 1.75 at 540x600 (baseline 6.05 to 6.55 and 1.79 to 2.38). 16 runs; the 4 that shared the machine with biome-electric-liquid's build were retried quiet. Fire 2.59 <= 2.95 target (was 4.34). DevShots High and Medium (menu, MidFill, PocketPending, CutDroplets) at 540x960, 1080x1200 and 1080x2400 have the same composition and checkpoints as docs/waveB/shots/gate/fire_* and gate/medium/fire_*. The intended changes are the flame band, the fill front, the coal tiers and the spark. One environmental difference: the shared SaveData 'Ta couleur' choice is yellow now, so the human plays yellow in most shots.

FireOverlay.hlsl shape 3 draws a white disc of 0.12 u at full alpha (held down to opacity 0.62), a pale white-hot corona to 0.17 u, and an orange #FF8A2A halo (linear 1.0, 0.254, 0.0232, alpha 0.8 out to 0.2 u, smooth to 0.45 u) under eight rays 1.5x longer. The HDR core on High is unchanged. All sizes are in world units through UV0.z, for the actors' 0.5 u glint quad (WaveC_FireSparkSignatureFitsTheActorsGlintQuad). FireFx keeps the live-front shower at most 20 sparks (WaveC_FireFxSparkBudgets; FireBiomeTests.Fire_EffectsRespectTheParticleCap green in the full EditMode run). FireBead caps the fireball's luminance at linear 0.7 below High. Acceptance: DevShot -quality medium fire CutDroplets at 540x960, counting luma >= 235 pixels within 1.5 u of the front against the human pearl (docs/waveC/actors/tools/measure.py). Orange human (build 19:08): 85 vs 22 = 3.86x. Final build with the yellow human: 164 vs 81 = 2.02x. Low with the yellow human: 1.95x (0.82x before the cap). My own 22 px window count on the orange shot: 66 vs 23. Crops: docs/waveC/biome-fire/spark_vs_fireball_medium_low_540.png shows a white star with an orange core and a dimmer yellow fireball.

The flame coordinate is the world distance d from the wide relief field (inverse normal CDF fit, Abramowitz and Stegun 26.2.23). WaveC_FireEdgeDistanceInvertsTheWideEdgeProfile checks |error| < 0.002 u from -0.7 to 1.2 u and checks that sigma matches the blur chain. With Gather, the normal is the gradient of the bilinearly interpolated distances, so it has no 2x2 quad steps. Reach is 0.3 to 0.85 u by edge orientation (bottom edges 0.3 u > 0.25 u). An inward band of upward tongues burns over the outer 0.42 to 0.5 u of the bed. Acceptance on DevShot fire 1080x1200 High MidFill (60 px/u; view 18 u wide): tongues rise about 40 to 50 px above top edges (docs/waveC/biome-fire/zoom_top_edge_1080_high.png) and 10 to 20 px below bottom and bottom-right edges (ruler_bottom_edge_1080_high.png, zoom_bottom_edge_1080_high.png). The critic measured 4 to 11 px and 0 px. The same band shows at 1080x2400 on High and on Medium (midfill_1080x2400_high_vs_medium.png). PocketPending at 540x960 on High, Medium and Low shows home (yellow coals and flames), the pending pocket (yellow ember stripes over the teal bed, no flames) and the teal rival clearly apart, in four distinct colors.

(1) The front is a band: a Gaussian of the age centred at 0.08 s, width 0.08 s, zero after 0.3 s. (2) Tongues rise from it with the flame noise: the reach grows up to +75 % with a white-hot base, and fresh embers glow warmer for 0.8 s. (3) Ages are gathered and clamped per texel (0.4 s band, 0.8 s warm) before interpolation, and the jitter is 0.05 u. (4) nOut comes from the Gather distance gradient on target 4.5. On the GLES3 target 2.0 path it now comes from the relief gradient (_PIO_TerritoryHeight .yz, decoded for the 8-bit fallback) wherever the relief slopes, which is where the gate and the owner tap are read; screen derivatives remain the fallback outside the beds. (5) The band position comes from the contour (d) and the age only gates it. Acceptance: a 12 fps desktop capture of the release player at 540x960 High (ffmpeg gdigrab over the topmost window, tools/seqcap.ps1; frames f0055 to f0066 in docs/waveC/biome-fire/seq_fire_fill_540_high.png). The white-hot band forms at the closing point, then crosses the loop with tongues licking ahead of it (f0061 to f0065, about 0.4 s after the DevShot's own MidFill pause), and the embers settle behind it. The whole sweep is within about 0.6 s. At 1080 (zoom_fire_fill_front_1080.png, compare docs/waveC/visuals/zoom_fire_fill_front_1080.png) the fresh coals are brighter, the boundary with older coals follows the dark crust, and there is no jagged seam. The GLES3 look itself is not visible on this Windows machine (compile verified only).

Low uses PIO_FireCellsStatic: a 2x2 jittered Voronoi with one hash per cell and static points, feeding the same coal and crust ramp as Medium. It never thresholds value noise. Twinkle picks a coal by its id hash and floor(time x 3) on every tier, with no value-noise dashes. DevShot -quality low fire at 540x960 PocketPending: coals read as cells like Medium, with no rounded squares, no contour rings and no 1 px dashes (docs/waveC/biome-fire/low_pocket_before_after_540.png, left the critic's ds_540_low_fire, right this build). Probe -fps 1000 -mute at 1080x1200, interleaved: Low 3.84 / 3.43 ms against Medium 3.95 / 4.07 ms (High 4.41 / 5.85), all PASS with hash 246577239DE179C4 (docs/waveC/biome-fire/perf/tier_*.log). Low is not above Medium (baseline Low 7.49 > Medium 6.05).

open_issues: Small hard-edged flame fragments can appear for one frame at a neck where the thread meets the bed during a fill. At 1080 High MidFill there is one, about 10 px, near the closing point, with a straight horizontal cut. Likely cause: where edges meet, the bilinear distance gradient (and so normalOk and the gate's sample point) steps at height-texel boundaries, and the fill gate's reach boost then jumps. It is not visible at 540 or in the 12 fps sequence. Left as is, to avoid a late change after the perf measurement.

The GLES3 target 2.0 path (no Gather) is verified by compilation only (WaveC_FireGraphsCompileOnEverySubshader). Its look (relief-gradient normal, gate ends snapping to cells) needs a device or GLES3 run at the gate.

The 1080x2400 shots come from resizing the window past the 1200 px monitor with MoveWindow (tools/tallshot.ps1); -screen-height alone is clamped to 1200. The 1080 acceptance numbers were taken at 1080x1200, the critic's size, at the same 60 px/u.
The human's color in DevShots follows the shared SaveData 'Ta couleur' choice, which is yellow on this machine now (orange in the gate shots). Spark ratios were measured with both colors.

Perf numbers come from a shared laptop. 4 of 16 perfslope runs overlapped biome-electric-liquid's build and were retried quiet. The gate should re-run perfslope on Build/Windows once all packages land.
